about: Topic index for Ved. Look a topic up before searching: jq '.topics.<name>' docs/index.json. Paths are relative to the repo root. Each topic lists where the code is, the symbols to grep for, its settings, the rules that bite, and its tests. Keep it current when files move.

status.phase_2_memory: done: conversations, people and birthdays, semantic search, document memory
status.phase_3_photos: skipped for now; waits for the home server. Plan: Immich plus a photos MCP server, not a custom build
status.phase_4_web_fast: done: web search and fetch, streaming, thinking state, acknowledgements, parallel tools
status.phase_5_voice: in progress: the local voice service (apps/voice: Kokoro text to speech, faster-whisper recognition) and the backend's /voice routes are built; the web client is wired separately
not_yet: phone access verified end to end (needs Tailscale)
status.home_server: noddy: containerised setup via ./ved server written, not yet run there; Cloudflare tunnel hostname and streaming through it unconfirmed; auth, unattended running and backups not built yet
status.per_user_data: done: users table, Access email picks the user, chats, memory, documents, people, reminders and push are per person; owner from VED_OWNER_EMAIL
status.claude_provider: done: Claude Haiku 5.5 through Anthropic's SDK behind VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, with the person's MCP connections exposed to it; Ved's connection-aware stamp and no-email labels; Settings shows Claude credit left, counted from each response's usage against an owner-entered balance.
status.family_directory: done: Ved reads the household directory from home-admin (VED_FAMILY_DIRECTORY_URL/TOKEN), knows who is speaking and replies in their language, lists the family in the system prompt, shares opt-in family notes (family.remember / family.notes) and shows it all under Settings > What Ved knows
status.private_notes: done: 'remember this just for me' saves a per-user private note (notes.remember / notes.recall); Settings > What Ved knows lists them above the family notes with Delete

agent-loop.summary: One loop serves both chat endpoints: model round, tools, repeat until an answer or the round cap.
rules: Both endpoints go through Agent._events; never fork the loop.
Tool failures return to the model as is_error, never raised.

The system prompt is SYSTEM_PROMPT plus the deterministic Family block (system_prompt_for); the current time, timezone, the signed-in user's line and default reply language ride on the latest user message, never in history or the system prompt.
Tool calls in one round run concurrently; outcomes go back in call order.

Agent.run and Agent.stream require user_id and user_line and take reply_language; user_id goes to toolbox calls and never into prompts or stored tool arguments. user_line is speaker_label(user, person): a name sentence, or an ask-for-the-name sentence, never the email.
The model sees a fixed tool list (VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS, sorted by name), never a per-message choice: Ollama reuses its cache only for an identical system prompt plus tools prefix.

The latest user line is stamped with the current time, the user line, a Default reply language line (when the directory knows the person's language) and a Connected apps line (non-built-in tool prefixes, from the same tools_for call the round uses). The system prompt tells the model to use these lines silently.

SYSTEM_PROMPT asks replies to follow the user's language and script (English, Telugu, Hindi or a mix); keep that sentence when editing the prompt. A Default reply language line from the family directory overrides that default.
AgentRequest.voice is the spoken-reply flag. It adds SPOKEN_REPLY_LINE to the per-turn stamp, never to the system prompt, and reaches Agent.run and Agent.stream unchanged.
Agent takes a FamilyDirectory (default NoFamilyDirectory) and reads it once per turn for the Family block; see the family topic.

streaming.summary: Replies stream over SSE: thinking, ack, token, tool, tool_result, then done or error.
rules: A streamed turn runs as a background task in TurnRegistry and saves its answer even if the client left.
A turn in one conversation waits on that conversation's lock, so turns never run concurrently.
A failed turn saves nothing; the server mints conversation_id only at save time.
Tool calls and recording are shielded from client disconnect.
fetch, not EventSource, because EventSource cannot POST.
Reasoning text is dropped in the provider; only a thinking event is sent.
Messages sent while busy queue in memory and send in order.

acknowledgements.summary: Instant phrase shown when the first model round is a tool call.
rules: A new tool domain gets a phrase here.

llm-provider.summary: The model sits behind LLMProvider: Ollama through the OpenAI /v1 shape today, or Claude Haiku 5.5 through Anthropic's SDK when VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic.
rules: No vendor SDK outside llm/.
A provider implements complete() and stream(); streamed tool calls arrive in fragments keyed by index.
Moving the model is a URL change, not a code change.
VED_LLM_TEMPERATURE=0.0; sampling corrupts tool arguments.
The model needs 'tools' in `ollama show <model>` capabilities.
Anthropic is the official SDK only (AsyncAnthropic, typed APIError classes); no shim, no raw HTTP. The SDK speaks httpx2, which is the httpx the project already uses.
Anthropic tool names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$: ToolNameMap maps each Ved name (memory.search) to a safe name per request and back; a collision gets a numeric suffix.

AssistantMessage.provider_content carries Anthropic's raw content blocks (thinking included) across tool rounds of one turn; it is excluded from model_dump and never stored, since history keeps only text and tool calls.
Anthropic requests send no temperature or thinking field; the system prompt is one cached text block.
VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic without VED_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fails at startup; the key is never sent to the embedder, which stays on VED_LLM_BASE_URL (Ollama).
Anthropic errors become LLMRequestError with a plain message: a 401 names VED_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a credit-balance 400 says the balance ran out, timeouts and unreachable hosts are named as such.

Each final Anthropic message reports its usage through on_usage (a UsageReporter passed to build_provider); a failing reporter logs a warning and never changes the reply. The llm package never imports the database: UsageStore.record is injected.

conversations.summary: Persisted threads; history replayed into each turn; listed and reopened in the UI.
rules: Order by sequence, never created_at.
Replay prompts and final answers only, never tool calls.
The server mints conversation_id, only after the model answers.
The open conversation is ?c=<id> via history.pushState; useSearchParams needs Suspense.
A conversation opened while answering polls status every 3 s and reloads when it finishes.
Every conversation belongs to a user; ConversationStore methods take user_id first and other users get ConversationNotFoundError (404).
TurnRegistry is keyed by (user_id, conversation_id).

reminders.summary: Create, list, reschedule and complete reminders; the scheduler fires them.
rules: Claimed FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with notified_at in the same transaction.
If nothing was reachable the stamp is cleared and it retries until give_up_after.
Prefer reschedule over complete-then-create.
due_at must carry a UTC offset.
When VED_PLAN_MCP_TOKEN is set, Ved's reminders server is not started; plan.create_reminder, plan.list_reminders, plan.my_due_reminders and plan.mark_reminder_done replace it.
Reminders belong to a user; the scheduler runs across all users and pushes each only to its owner.

push.summary: Web Push delivery of reminders and check-ins to subscribed browsers.
rules: Sends carry a socket timeout, an asyncio deadline and a 24h TTL.
404/410 subscriptions are deleted, not retried.
VAPID keys live only in gitignored .env; the generator refuses to overwrite.
Needs a secure context: localhost or real HTTPS.
Subscriptions belong to a user; send(user_id, notification) reaches only that user's devices.

read-aloud.summary: Replies read aloud and voice dictation. When Ved's server reports a voice (GET /voice/status), replies are spoken by the server's neural voice through the shared audio engine; otherwise the device's own speech engines (speechSynthesis and SpeechRecognition) are used. Telugu and Hindi sentences use the device voice unless the server speaks that language.
settings: ved.voice (localStorage): autoRead, voiceName, teluguVoiceName, hindiVoiceName, rate (0.8-1.4), pitch (0.8-1.3), listenLang (en-IN, te-IN, hi-IN, en-US), autoSend, serverVoiceName (server voice id, null for the server default), serverSpeed (0.8-1.3)
rules: Server voice, when /voice/status lists tts_languages: replies go to POST /voice/speak through the one shared AudioContext (getVoicePlayer). Speech text leaves the device only in that case. Recognition is then done by POST /voice/transcribe in talk mode; the browser's SpeechRecognition is the fallback when stt is false.
Without a server voice, speech stays on device: speechSynthesis and SpeechRecognition are the browser's or OS's engines, and the Voice card says recognition may go to Apple or Google.

A sentence in Telugu or Hindi script goes to the device voice when the server does not list that language, and is skipped when the device has no voice for it. A server error on one sentence falls back to the device voice for that sentence.

iOS allows audio only after a user gesture. getVoicePlayer().unlock() runs on the first pointerdown or keydown in the app and on every talk or read-aloud tap, creating or resuming the AudioContext and playing a silent sample. Device speech unlocks with an empty utterance as before.
Auto-read and the per-reply speaker button use the same engine as talk mode when a server voice is on. Auto-read never speaks replies sent from talk mode, because talk mode speaks them itself.
Speech stops on a new send, a new or switched conversation (Chat remounts), and when the page is hidden.
Settings → Voice shows the server voice picker, speed and Test voice only when the server voice is on; device controls sit under a subsection headed Device voice.
Helpers in speech-text.ts, speech-voice.ts, speech-stream.ts (cutSentences) and audio-level.ts are pure. The web client has no test runner yet, so they are checked by running them directly.

talk-mode.summary: Hands-free talk with Ved: a full-screen overlay that listens, sends each utterance as a normal turn with voice: true, and speaks the reply sentence by sentence while it streams.
settings: Talk shows only when /voice/status reports stt true and the browser can record (MediaRecorder and getUserMedia).
rules: The Talk button replaces the dictation mic in the composer and sits on the welcome screen when talk is available. Without stt the old browser dictation mic stays.

Each utterance: getUserMedia with echo cancellation and noise suppression. The MediaRecorder starts as soon as listening starts, so leading silence is recorded; VAD only decides when to stop: speech is heard at SPEECH_LEVEL, then stop after 1.2 s of quiet or 30 s. No speech within 8 s stops and discards the take (an empty listen). The server's Whisper runs with a VAD filter.
Two empty listens in a row (silence or an empty transcript) pause the loop with Tap to talk. A microphone error pauses it with the reason.
A turn waits until the chat is not busy, then calls the normal send path with voice: true, so the turn appears in the conversation like any other message. Auto-read is skipped for talk turns.
Speech starts after the first complete sentence of the streamed reply (., ?, !, । or a newline followed by space). A tool call breaks the segment; the rest is spoken at the end.
Tapping the emblem interrupts Ved: speech stops, the reply keeps streaming into the chat unspoken, and listening starts at once. Tapping while paused resumes.
The loop stops on End, Escape, the page becoming hidden, or unmount. A new turn never starts after the loop has stopped.
The mic level and the playback level drive the rings through the --level CSS variable, written from requestAnimationFrame. Reduced motion skips the loop and keeps the rings still.

After each listen the mic stream is stopped (every track) and dropped before Ved speaks, and the shared AudioContext is woken. On iPhone a live getUserMedia stream routes playback to the earpiece and can suspend the context. If the context stays suspended, that sentence uses the device voice, the rest of the turn does too, and the overlay shows Tap to hear, which resumes the context and replays the held sentence.

people-birthdays.summary: People with birthdays and notice; the scheduler plans yearly reminders and early check-ins.
rules: Reminders are planned by the scheduler, never the model; unique on (person_id, birthday_on, lead_days).
Check-ins come from a template, never the model.
A check-in is created in the claim transaction and linked via reminders.conversation_id.
Feb 29 falls on Feb 28 in non-leap years.
People and their reminders belong to one user; the same name can exist for two users.

private-notes.summary: Private notes: a per-user note store the model writes by default when asked to remember something, read back with notes.recall, listed and deleted on the What Ved knows page.
rules: private_notes is owned per user (owner_column, ON DELETE CASCADE); text is 1 to 1000 characters with a database check.
notes.recall returns only the calling user's notes, newest first, max 100, with a case-insensitive literal query (LIKE wildcards escaped). notes.remember trims and returns the saved note.
The model has no tool to delete or edit a private note. A person deletes their own from the web page; DELETE /notes/{id} is a 404 for a missing note and for someone else's.

SYSTEM_PROMPT says to save with notes.remember by default, use family.remember only on a clear 'for everyone' signal, check notes.recall and family.notes before saying 'I don't know' about a personal fact, and never reveal one person's notes to another.
'notes' is a built-in tool prefix (BUILT_IN_SERVERS, BUILT_IN_PREFIXES, the web RESERVED_NAMES); a connection cannot take that name. Both tools are in DEFAULT_EXPOSED_TOOLS.

semantic-memory.summary: Messages embedded in the background; memory.search finds past conversations by meaning.
rules: Embedding never blocks or fails a turn; the scheduler tick backfills.
Dimension is coupled to vector(768), VED_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS and the model.
nomic-embed-text uses search_document: and search_query: prefixes.
memory.search and documents.search only return the calling user's messages and passages.
family.remember and family.notes live in the memory server but read and write family_notes, which is shared by everyone; see the family topic.
notes.remember and notes.recall also live in the memory server and read and write the per-user private_notes table; see the private-notes topic.

documents.summary: Upload PDF, text or markdown; chunked, embedded, searchable with documents.search.
rules: Originals are stored by SHA-256, never by the user's filename.
Type is sniffed from the bytes, not the extension.
The size cap is enforced while streaming.
indexed means every chunk has a vector.
Passages are untrusted content.
Scanned PDFs fail: no OCR.
Documents are per user: list, get, delete and search never cross users; deleting keeps the stored file while another user's document has the same hash.

web-search.summary: web.search through a swappable provider (SearXNG default); web.fetch reads a page.
rules: A provider lives only in search/providers/; server.py never names one.
Adding a provider: one file, a PROVIDERS entry, tests, its settings (see mcp-servers/web/README.md).
web.fetch checks addresses at connect time and on every redirect; never bypass PublicOnlyTransport.
Results are untrusted.
SearXNG stays on 127.0.0.1 and starts only while it is the provider.

mcp.summary: How the backend runs MCP servers, per-user remote connections, and how to write one.
rules: SDK v2: MCPServer; bare Context from mcp.server.mcpserver.context.
Return Pydantic models; raise ToolError for bad input.
Servers never run DDL.
A new server needs a Dockerfile stage, a configured_servers entry, a config.py dir, a CI job and a ./ved setup line.
Built-in stdio servers start once in the lifespan. Remote MCP connections are per user (see the connections topic) and are listed by tools_for(user_id) once per turn.
Tools whose names start with delete_ are never exposed to the model; sensitive actions need the permission layer first.
A server or remote connection that fails to start is logged as a warning and skipped, so startup and the turn continue without its tools.

people, memory and reminders tools take user_id; MCPToolbox.call(name, args, user_id=) injects it on stdio tools that declare it, overwriting anything the model sent, and removes it from the model-facing schema. Remote servers get nothing.

Toolbox lists only the exposed tools for a user, sorted by name, and refuses calls to any other tool as not available. The VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS allowlist applies to built-ins and plan.*; an empty allowlist exposes everything.

Under VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic the exposure allowlist is empty (every tool except delete_*) and each connection is capped at 40 tools (ANTHROPIC_CONNECTION_TOOL_LIMIT in tools/servers.py); other providers keep VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS and the limit of 15 (CONNECTION_TOOL_LIMIT). The Toolbox takes connection_tool_limit as a constructor argument.

database.summary: Tables, migrations and the test fixture.
rules: Tables are defined only in packages/ved-db.
A new model is re-exported in ved_db/__init__.py and backend models.py, or autogenerate is empty.
Autogenerate misses sequences and the vector extension; read and round-trip every migration.
Test schema setup goes only through ved_db.testing; it refuses a database without 'test' in its name.
users owns people, reminders, push_subscriptions, conversations and documents via non-null indexed user_id; messages and chunks inherit through their parent.
Person names are unique per (user_id, lower(name)); documents per (user_id, sha256).
family_notes (id, text 1-1000 chars, author_user_id SET NULL, created_at) is shared across users, not owned by one; it has no user_id owner column.

connector.summary: The web client's only backend client; framework-free.
rules: No React or Next imports.
Components call connector.*, never fetch.
HttpError surfaces the backend's detail message.
conversationStatus reads GET /conversations/{id}/status.
speak returns an ArrayBuffer: a request with binary: true reads the response with arrayBuffer() instead of parsing JSON or text.
transcribe sends multipart field audio (filename from the blob type: webm, mp4 or ogg) and an optional language field.
voice: true is sent only on talk-mode turns; other requests keep the old body.
endpoints: POST /agent/message/stream and POST /agent/message accept voice: true

rules: Check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing Next code.

The emblem (VedEmblem in ved-emblem.tsx) follows the chat's pending or streaming state: thinking until the first reply token, speaking while text streams, and a 28 px avatar beside the in-flight reply only. Completed replies get no avatar. Its animations are CSS transforms and opacity only, and reduced motion keeps only a glow fade.
Markdown replies never render raw HTML.
Icons are generated from assets/ved-mark.png.
The install banner is app-wide. It is hidden when standalone, after appinstalled, and for 14 days after ✕.
The manifest is served from /app-manifest with crossOrigin=use-credentials, not from a metadata manifest entry.
The browser calls /api; next.config.ts rewrites /api/* to the backend, so the container serves one origin. Rewrite destinations are fixed at build time.
compress is off so the rewrite does not gzip the SSE reply stream. Streaming through the tunnel is not confirmed yet; check it on the server.
The connector accepts a relative base URL such as /api and resolves it against the page origin.

The typing indicator (TypingIndicator in chat.tsx) shows three CSS-animated dots from send until the first reply text, with the tool, acknowledgement or thinking label beside them, and in the answering placeholder after a refresh. It has role=status and aria-label="Ved is typing", and reduced motion swaps the bounce for an opacity pulse.

Connections lives in Settings (/settings#integrations); /connections redirects there. It calls connector.* only, shows a per-connection on/off switch, Test and Remove, and offers the Plan and MyFinances presets or a custom server.

The home top bar holds conversations, new conversation and a gear to /settings, plus a backend status dot whose tooltip and aria-label carry the full status text. The reminder banner appears only while reminders are off or failed and links to /settings#notifications.
Settings (/settings) has sections Integrations, What Ved knows, Claude usage, Notifications, Install app, Appearance, Voice and About, in that order; each section id is a hash target.

The theme is stored under localStorage key ved.theme (system, light or dark). THEME_INIT_SCRIPT in the layout head sets data-theme before paint; globals.css lets data-theme override prefers-color-scheme.
The mic and speaker controls exist only when the browser supports them; see the read-aloud topic.

phone-access.summary: Reach Ved from a phone privately over Tailscale serve.
rules: tailscale serve only, never Funnel.
Unverified until Tailscale is installed.

infra.summary: Docker Compose, the ved script, CI.
rules: Every port binds to 127.0.0.1.
SearXNG is behind the 'search' compose profile.
./ved api reads apps/backend/.env; the container reads infra/.env; never run both.
Postgres 18 volume is /var/lib/postgresql.
Corporate-network CA steps are no-ops on a personal machine.
The ollama service is behind the server compose profile, publishes no port and is capped at 4.5 GB.
compose.server.yaml is the only file that attaches services to the external 'home' network; ./ved server passes it, nothing else does.
The web and backend containers use container_name ved-web and ved-backend; the tunnel reaches ved-web:3000 on home.
The voice service (ved-voice, apps/voice) publishes no port and is capped at 1536 MB. It is in the default profile, so ./ved server builds and starts it.

The backend reaches home-admin at http://home-admin:3470/api/family over the 'home' network; ./ved set-family-token <file> writes VED_FAMILY_DIRECTORY_TOKEN into infra/.env and restarts the backend. ./ved server copies FAMILY_DIRECTORY_TOKEN from ~/home-admin/.env (VED_HOME_ADMIN_ENV) when it differs, so deploys set it up without a shell.

server.summary: Running Ved on the home server: Ubuntu, i5, DDR3 (16 GB max), three hard disks, no GPU.
rules: The ved script runs on macOS (Colima) and Linux (native Docker); detect with is_macos, never assume.
On the server set VED_LLM_MODEL to a model that fits 16 GB (granite4.1:3b); qwen3.6:35b needs ~23 GB.
Corporate CA steps are macOS-only and no-ops on Linux.
Backups go on a different disk from Postgres's data.
Unattended running, auto-deploy and backups are not built yet.
The server is noddy: i7-10510U, 7.5 GB RAM, no GPU. ./ved server is the containerised path; the bare-metal steps are older notes.
./ved server refuses to run on macOS. Its default chat model is qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M because qwen3.6:35b does not fit.
Migrations run in the backend container with docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend alembic upgrade head.

./ved set-anthropic-key <file> stores the key (must start with sk-ant-) in infra/.env, sets VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic and VED_LLM_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5, restarts the backend, then stops the local chat model in Ollama to free memory. It never prints the key.
./ved use-local-model switches back to openai-compatible with the server's local model (SERVER_MODEL) and restarts the backend; it does not pull the model, so run ./ved server first if it is missing.
While VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, ./ved server does not overwrite VED_LLM_MODEL or pull the chat model; it still pulls the embedding model.

auth.summary: Cloudflare Access sign-in check: the backend verifies the JWT Access sends and admits only listed admin emails. Off on the Mac.
rules: VED_AUTH defaults to off; with cloudflare-access every route except /health needs a valid Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion token.
Only RS256 tokens from the team's certs endpoint are accepted; audience and issuer must match, and emails match case-insensitively.
Refusals are 401 JSON {detail: reason}; the reason names what to fix in settings.
Identity: require_access returns the verified AccessResult (email, name); current_user turns it into a users row, or the owner when auth is off.

users.summary: Per-person data: every chat, memory, document, person, reminder and push device belongs to a user picked by the Access email.
rules: Every route that touches data takes CurrentUser; stores take user_id first and filter by it.
Another user's conversation or document is a 404, including GET /conversations/{id}/status.
With VED_AUTH=off every request acts as the owner (VED_OWNER_EMAIL, default owner@ved.local), created if missing.
Emails are stored lowercase; the user is created on first sign-in.
The migration creates the owner from VED_OWNER_EMAIL (process env) and backfills every existing row to it.
Names (people) and file hashes (documents) are unique per user; stored files are shared by hash, so delete unlinks only when no document references it.
Birthday reminders and check-ins inherit the person's owner; push goes only to the owner's subscriptions.
A push endpoint belongs to one user; subscribing from another account moves it.
MCP connections belong to one user and are listed, tested, changed and deleted only by that user.

speaker_label never returns the email: a person found in the family directory is 'You are talking with {directory name} (the owner's {relation}).', otherwise a named user is 'You are talking with {name}.' and an unnamed one gets a line asking for the name once and saving it with people.remember (there is no memory save tool). See the family topic.

connections.summary: Per-person MCP connections: each user links Plan, MyFinances or a custom MCP server; tokens are encrypted and tools are prefixed by connection name.
rules: Connection tokens are Fernet-encrypted with VED_SECRET_KEY and never returned; responses carry has_token only.
Without VED_SECRET_KEY, connection writes return 503 and only the owner's VED_PLAN_MCP_TOKEN fallback is served.
Every connection query filters by user_id; another person's connection is a 404.
Names are 2-20 lowercase slugs and may not be a built-in prefix (memory, documents, family, web, people, reminders).
A connection's name is its tool prefix; delete_* tools from any remote server are never exposed.
plan keeps the VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS allowlist; other connections expose non-destructive tools in name order, capped at 15 (40 under anthropic).
A user with an enabled plan connection (or the owner fallback) has Ved's reminders.* tools hidden from the model; the reminders server still runs.
Remote sessions are cached per (user, connection) for five minutes; each runs in its own task so it opens and closes in one task.

Presets (PRESETS in connections.py) are one-click starting points: Plan, MyFinances, Snappy (photos, http://ved-mcp-snappy:8200/mcp), TV remote (host.docker.internal:8766) and home-admin. The backend container maps host.docker.internal to the host gateway so the TV remote is reachable.
A preset is only a name, URL and help line; the user still pastes their own token, and the connection is tested like any other.

claude-usage.summary: Claude credit left: Ved counts its own spend from each response's usage and subtracts it from the balance the owner types in.
rules: Anthropic has no balance API for this key: spend is counted from each final message's usage (input, cache write, cache read, output) and priced by llm/pricing.py, per million tokens, with the higher rates above 100,000 prompt tokens.

The balance is typed in by the owner (PUT /usage/claude/balance, 0 to 10,000, copied from the Anthropic Console). Remaining is the balance minus spend since the balance was set, floored at 0. Without a balance the card shows spend from the beginning.
Only the owner can set the balance (403 otherwise); every signed-in user can read it.
llm_usage is shared, not per user, because Ved is the only client of its API key. Today and this month use VED_TIMEZONE, so the day starts at local midnight.
Usage is tracked only for VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic; the card says the local model costs nothing otherwise.
A model missing from the pricing table is recorded with no cost, so it adds nothing to the totals.

snappy.summary: snappy, the user's photo app: a read-only MCP server over streamable HTTP where each person sends their own snappy API key.
rules: Runs as its own container (ved-mcp-snappy) on the default network, port 8200, path /mcp; no published ports.
Every request needs Authorization: Bearer <snappy API key>; no token is a 401 before MCP runs. The key is forwarded to snappy as x-api-key and never stored or logged.
Read-only: no tool writes to snappy. Photo links are {SNAPPY_PUBLIC_URL}/photos/{id}.
Results are capped at 50 photos per call and named people and albums at 50 per list.
Person and album names match case-insensitively; an ambiguous person name asks for the full name instead of guessing.
Only read tools are exposed; the photos server never calls a write endpoint.

voice-service.summary: Local neural voice and speech recognition: Kokoro text to speech and faster-whisper transcription in apps/voice, reached only through the backend's /voice routes.
endpoints: ved-voice: GET /status, GET /voices, POST /speak (JSON text, voice, speed; returns audio/wav), POST /transcribe (multipart audio, form language en|hi|te|auto)
backend: GET /voice/status, GET /voice/voices, POST /voice/speak, POST /voice/transcribe; all need CurrentUser
rules: Speech stays on the home server. Audio and text never go to a cloud engine; a cloud engine is a new module behind SpeechSynthesizer or SpeechRecognizer plus a setting.
ved-voice publishes no port. Only the backend reaches it at http://ved-voice:8300 on the compose network.
Models are pinned by URL and sha256 in apps/voice/Dockerfile and baked into the image at build time. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 keeps runtime from downloading anything.
Kokoro voices offered are English (a*, b*) and Hindi (h*). Kokoro has no Telugu voice, so Telugu is recognition only.
Text is stripped of markup and emoji, then split into sentences and synthesised in order into one WAV. The text limit is 1500 characters.
Uploads are capped at 10 MB and 60 seconds. The container is sniffed from magic bytes (WAV, WebM, Ogg, MP4/M4A), not from the content type the browser sends.
Inference runs in threads behind semaphores (speech 2, transcription 1) so the event loop stays free.
The backend's /voice/status answers 200 with stt false and no voices when the service is unreachable. Other failures are 503, or the service's own status when it rejects a request.
A spoken reply is AgentRequest.voice. It adds SPOKEN_REPLY_LINE to the per-turn stamp, never to the cached system prompt.

family.summary: Ved knows the family: a cached read-only directory from home-admin, who is speaking, the Family block in the system prompt, opt-in shared family notes, and the What Ved knows page.
rules: The directory is home-admin's GET /api/family with a Bearer token. Relations are relative to the owner (relation "self"). An empty VED_FAMILY_DIRECTORY_TOKEN turns the feature off and the directory is empty.

FamilyDirectory is a Protocol (current, aclose). HomeAdminFamilyDirectory fetches with a 3 s timeout, caches 5 minutes, keeps the last good copy on any error and waits 30 s before retrying a failure. It never logs the token or emails.

A signed-in user is matched to a directory person by email, case-insensitively. A match changes speaker_label to 'You are talking with {name} (the owner's {relation}).', sets User.name once when it is empty (UserDirectory.adopt_name, never overwrites) and passes the person's language (en, te, hi) to Agent as reply_language. No email ever reaches a prompt or a label.
reply_language adds a 'Default reply language' line to the per-turn stamp, after the user line, so spoken replies follow it too. The Telugu name says Telugu script.

The system prompt is SYSTEM_PROMPT plus the Family block (system_prompt_for), identical for every speaker and turn while the directory is unchanged: owner first, then by name; nicknames sorted; names, nicknames, relation to the owner and birthday day and month only, no emails or ids. Per-speaker facts ride on the stamp, never in the system prompt, so prompt caching holds.

SYSTEM_PROMPT teaches nicknames and relative relations, never revealing one person's conversations, memory, documents, people or reminders to another, and that family notes are saved only on a clear 'for everyone' signal and the model says what it saved; anything else goes to private notes (see the private-notes topic).

family_notes is shared and global: anyone reads every note (family.notes, max 100, newest first, case-insensitive query, author display name), the author is users.name or 'Someone'. author_user_id is SET NULL when a user is deleted. Text is 1 to 1000 characters.

The model has no tool to delete or edit a family note. A person deletes their own note from the web page (DELETE /family/notes/{id}): 404 when it does not exist, 403 when someone else wrote it or its author is gone.
GET /family returns people (name, nicknames, relation, birthday month and day, language), me (the caller's match or null) and owner_name. It never returns emails or birth years.

Settings > What Ved knows (/settings#what-ved-knows) shows who Ved thinks you are, the family list and the notes; empty directory shows 'Ved doesn't know your family yet. The household admin can add people in home-admin.'
'family' is a built-in tool prefix (BUILT_IN_SERVERS, BUILT_IN_PREFIXES); a connection cannot take that name. ./ved set-family-token <file> stores the token in infra/.env on the server.
